2608.19804.title: ADAPT: Physics-Aware Diffusion-based World Models for Adaptive Predictive Transferable HVAC Control
2608.19804.paper_summary: Buildings account for roughly one-third of global energy consumption and CO$_2$ emissions. Optimizing indoor climate systems plays a critical role for urban climate mitigation aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals 11 and 13. However, indoor delayed thermodynamic responses and partial observability severely hinder existing methods, which are primarily limited by implicit thermal inertia, occupancy dynamic prediction, and cumulative prediction errors, especially for out-of-distribution environments. In practice, these challenges are further exacerbated by the high cost and privacy burden of dense indoor sensing, forcing operators to collect only limited data in a single operating regime while expecting controllers to generalize reliably across unseen seasons and climate regions. To address this problem, we propose ADAPT, a physics-aware conditional diffusion indoor environmental world model for HVAC control. The model predicts a short-horizon held-action thermal baseline to capture the latent thermal inertia of the buildings. The diffusion backbone utilizes the robustness of generative models, while a learnable multi-zone heat-balance regularizer constrains generated trajectories to satisfy transferable building thermodynamics without requiring known building geometry or manually calibrated thermal parameters. A credit assignment is then design for the downstream reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments on SemibuildingSim and Sinergym demonstrate that ADAPT reduces HVAC energy consumption by 7.3\% and occupant discomfort by 30.2\% compared with state-of-the-art baselines under IID control. Under OOD control scenarios spanning unseen seasons and climate regions, ADAPT maintains robust performance with only marginal degradation relative to its IID performance, substantially outperforming existing methods in transfer robustness.
2608.19804.paper_summary_zh: 建築物約佔全球能源消耗和二氧化碳排放的三分之一。優化室內氣候系統在與聯合國可持續發展目標11和13相一致的城市氣候緩解中扮演著關鍵角色。然後，室內延遲的熱力學反應和部分可觀察性嚴重阻礙了現有方法，這些方法主要受到隱性熱慣性、佔用動態預測和累積預測誤差的限制，尤其是在分佈外環境中。在實踐中，這些挑戰因為高成本和密集室內感測的隱私負擔而進一步加劇，迫使操作員僅在單一操作範疇內收集有限數據，同時期望控制器能在未見的季節和氣候區域中可靠地進行泛化。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了ADAPT，一種面向物理的條件擴散室內環境世界模型，用於HVAC控制。該模型預測短期持有行動的熱基線，以捕捉建築物的潛在熱慣性。擴散骨幹利用生成模型的穩健性，而可學習的多區域熱平衡正則化器則約束生成的軌跡，以滿足可轉移的建築熱力學，而無需已知的建築幾何或手動校準的熱參數。然後設計了一個信用分配，用於下游強化學習。在SemibuildingSim和Sinergym上的廣泛實驗顯示，與最先進的基準相比，ADAPT在IID控制下將HVAC能源消耗降低了7.3\%，佔用者不適感降低了30.2\%。在跨越未見季節和氣候區域的OOD控制場景下，ADAPT保持了穩健的性能，相對於其IID性能僅有輕微的降級，顯著超越了現有方法在轉移穩健性方面的表現。
